top_choice_rationale: Circuit QED answers a sharply posed question, whether a single microwave photon can be coupled strongly and coherently to a solid-state artificial atom, with a 2004 theory proposal and first experiments that are mature, widely reproduced and now the basis of superconducting quantum technology and dispersive readout. The three-person allocation is clean and the citation scope is well bounded, and the 2025 prize did not cover this work. The optical lattice clock (P002) is an equally mature and cleanly credited second choice. The Higgs proposal (P003) is a major discovery but its three-name credit across two collaborations of thousands cannot be defended without excluding Gianotti and others, so it ranks below both; I still prefer it to no award.
